title: Add post-light function in spatial shaders for all renderers (useful in toon shading)

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: Add a post-light function named `compose()` to spatial shaders, and allow light functions to modify varyings assigned in `fragment()`. This closes [proposal#484](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/484) and [proposal#10527](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10527). This pull request supersedes [pull request #102708](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102708) with additional support for decal, SSR, and SSS effects. And this pull request takes a different approach to implement the feature in compatibility renderer. # Renderer Support - Forward+: Fully supported - Mobile: Fully supported - Compatibility: Supported with limitation: the `compose()` function would only be aware of lights without shadow (see below for discussion about this). # Feature Description This feature allows users to implement a `void compose()` function in spatial shaders, overriding the logic after `light()` has been executed. This function has access to the accumulated `DIFFUSE_LIGHT`, `SPECULAR_LIGHT`, along with decal-affected surface properties such as `ALBEDO`, `METALLIC`, `ROUGHNESS`, and `NORMAL`. Additionally, varyings assigned in `fragment()` can be reassigned in `light()` to accumulate arbitrary data and later read in `compose()`. Note that the first assignment is restricted to `fragment()`, so that unlit fragments does not generate undefined values. The `compose()` function has 3 output variables: `DIFFUSE_COLOR`, `SPECULAR_COLOR` and `ALPHA` (optional). This is to support effects that require separated specular pipeline, such as SSR and SSS. When not using separated specular, these 2 output variables are summed up to produce the output fragment color. Demonstration of the implemented feature (The godot icon is projected onto the sphere using a decal. Surface properties modified by the decal are accessible in `compose()`): | Forward+ | Mobile | Compatibility | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | The test project is here: [post_light_demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23776681/post_light_demo.zip) # About the Compatibility Renderer The `DIFFUSE_LIGHT` and `SPECULAR_LIGHT` inputs of `compose()` won't be aware of shadow-enabled light sources in compatibility renderer. This generates discrepancy between renderers. But I think this is acceptable for this pull request, for compatibility renderer inherently lacks the ability to properly handle non-additive lighting logic. With certain logic in `light()` function, the compatibility renderer already behaves very differently than other renderers prior to this pull request. Here's an example: The shader code: ``` shader_type spatial; // This shader demonstrates how the compatibility renderer is inherently limited // when doing non-additive lighting. void light() { bool surface_lit = DIFFUSE_LIGHT.x > 0.1; if (surface_lit) { DIFFUSE_LIGHT = vec3(dot(NORMAL, LIGHT) <= 0.0 ? 0.2 : 0.0); } else { DIFFUSE_LIGHT = vec3(dot(NORMAL, LIGHT) > 0.0 ? 0.2 : 0.0); } } ``` The effects: | Shadow Off | Shadow of Direct Light set to On | | --- | --- | | | | ## Explanation of this behavior: The compatibility renderer handles light sources with shadow by drawing the object multiple times, each time for a different light. During the first pass, no shadow-enabled light is taken into account, only shadowless light are handled. If there are any shadow-enabled light affecting the object, then there will be second and third passes to draw those lights, with additive blend mode. During drawing of these light passes, `DIFFUSE_LIGHT` and `SPECULAR_LIGHT` in `light()` are initialized to 0. As a result, `light()` functions would only behave in a way similar to other renderers if it is always doing `DIFFUSE/SPECULAR_LIGHT += xxx`. Otherwise, the math would break. (The shader here checks if the fragment is facing the light, if yes, it flips the `DIFFUSE_LIGHT` variable between 0.0 and 0.2. It is somewhat artificial to make the effect more obvious. But the idea applies to simpler and more common reduction strategies such as max()) That being said, compatibility renderer is currently unable to handle specialized shading logic that involves non-additive accumulation of light. Unless [proposal#8050](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8050) is implemented (but that would very likely result in some performance hit). Since compatibility renderer is inherently limited when doing specialized light reduction logic, I think the current measure in this pull request may be acceptable. For it does not introduce fundamentally new discrepancy between different renderers, and still implements the feature for compatibility to a certain degree. # Side Notes The `FINAL_FOG` variable is defined as `(color, density)` and is intended to be used like mix(original_color, FINAL_FOG.rgb, FINAL_FOG.a). Under the hood, some special handling is done for Forward+ to convert to this convention. It is named as `FINAL_FOG` instead of `FOG` because the name `FOG` triggers a define which overrides the vanilla fog. A somewhat more elegant solution *may* be to extend the gd shader compiler to additionally check the current stage when generating defines. But that would be more work, and it seems to be much more risky (it is used in too many places). # Discussions Currently, I put a commented-out `compose()` in the new shader template, with a brief description about its functionality, similar to `light()`. Is it better to write a commented one-liner resembling the original logic, so that users could quickly understand what's happening in vanilla implementation? The vanilla implementation integrates everything up, including metallic and fog. I am afraid some of these may be easy to miss for users who are not *that* familiar with the rendering pipeline of godot. Adding such things may serve as a good reminder, so that users are less likely to forget some term by accident and left wondering why things are not working.
